statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-16239 (PostgreSQL type confusion in cursor CLOSE + DECLARE executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.15: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16239/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, include it. Alpine's postgresql16 16.15-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 16.15 and lists CVE-2026-16239 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 16 release. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, which ships in the postgresql16 package. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases, their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine's secfixes do not list this CVE for them, so they are recorded as affected; 16.15-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-16239 (PostgreSQL type confusion in cursor CLOSE + DECLARE executes arbitrary code) affects PostgreSQL 18 releases before 18.6 and is fixed in PostgreSQL 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16239/. The PostgreSQL 18.6 release notes list it: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, and say that 18.5 was never released. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD records it under its 18.5-r0 secfixes entry: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are published at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64, each built from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We unpacked every one of these builds on both architectures. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres in the postgresql18 package, and its version banner in each build matches the package version. There is no 18.5-r0 build, so 18.6-r0 is the first published build carrying the fix. 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0 are built from earlier PostgreSQL 18 releases and are affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-16239, type confusion in the portal (cursor) lifecycle that lets a user execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database by re-creating a cursor or other portal with different types, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16239/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-16239. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
